title: Wood, hard rubber and metal clarinets
summary: Hall prefers solid wood for tone, tried a metal Vegan clarinet, and his wooden Selmer cracked.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Yeah, the wooden is the best. That way you get a good instrument, and the cheapest instrument, it may be made by the same company, but it's cheaper than the next one. Some of them are made out of hard rubber. But when you get solid wood, you know what I mean? It's better, and the oil of the clarinet is better than the tone.
Yeah. You really notice the difference in the tone, huh? Oh, yeah. Hard rubber, sure. Did you ever play a metal one? Yeah. Did you ever play a metal one?

A metal? Yeah. I had, I turned it back to the company. I didn't like it. It was a vegan too. They make them in Boston. Now you see this clarinet you got there? Yeah. That's part hard rubber. Yeah, that's part rubber. I have the one that I have, I have a German made clarinet, and it's solid wood. I got a selmer as wood. That's the reason why it cracked them. And that clarinet would never crack.
My selmer clarinet cracked because it's wood.
